analysis:
No concrete security regression found. The PR changes the SSD prefix-cache file coordination (T-041, SEC-035, A-001) with no crypto, HMAC-naming, salt-scoping, KEK or epoch changes.

Changed behavior checked:
- SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator becomes shared/exclusive with FIFO fairness. A queued writer blocks later readers. tryUpgrade/downgrade and tryAcquire keep maintenance and eviction skipping any file a reader holds. Stage reads use .shared (SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Read.swift:126-129, 201-204). The default access mode stays exclusive.
- SSDHybridCheckpointStore+ReadAttempt.swift: corrupt-file removal runs only through whileSoleHolder (lines ~96-120). A busy corrupt file can stay indexed until a reader finds it alone, a writer validates it, or it expires. That is an availability and cleanup delay only. AES-GCM/AAD authentication still rejects the bytes. The mtime touch is throttled to ttlSeconds/30 and runs before the second openChain records identity, so receipts stay valid.
- unusedSince is plumbed through SSDBlockIndex.swift (lastAccess accessor, protocol, retireActiveEntries), +Maintenance.swift and SSDPrefixCache.swift (~1790-1800). SSDWholeRootMaintainer's TTL sweep passes now-ttl. A loaded store keeps a file only if its in-memory last hit is within the TTL window and persists that hit as mtime. This is sliding-TTL consistent and does not exceed the 30-minute bound.
- Budget LRU eviction still orders by mtime and does not pass unusedSince. The unloaded-model fallback still deletes by mtime, which is conservative.
- Docs, changelog and tests are consistent with this behavior and do not weaken authentication assertions.

Unverified (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove, the SSDDiskBudget.retireActiveEntries implementation, SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator internals beyond the shown patch, and ~82 omitted units):
- whether files kept by unusedSince are correctly excluded from the returned removed set;
- whether the index lastAccess can only move forward, so no entry outlives the TTL;
- whether a persistent reader can starve TTL or budget retirement (a local DoS; T-060-style, bounded by lease semantics).

These are open integration questions, not findings.
